headline: Chugach State Park and Coastal Trail Access
reservation: While the city is open, specific activities like Kenai Fjords tours from Seward or specialized glamping sites require individual bookings months ahead for summer. Check Alaska State Parks for parking fee requirements at trailheads like Glen Alps; systems are subject to change.

days.title: Coastal Vistas and Native Heritage

stops.name: Tony Knowles Coastal Trail
stops.detail: Walk the paved shoreline path for views of Cook Inlet and potential sightings of local moose.

stops.name: Alaska Native Heritage Center
stops.detail: Learn about the traditions and contemporary lives of the 11 major cultural groups of Alaska.

days.driving: Local transfers under 20 minutes; allow time for trail parking
days.note: Stay off the tidal mudflats at all times due to dangerous silt and rapid tides.

days.title: Mountain Horizons and Alpine Tundra

stops.name: Glen Alps Trailhead
stops.detail: Access the gateway to Chugach State Park for views over the city and the Alaska Range.

stops.name: Powerline Pass
stops.detail: Follow the wide, relatively flat trail through a dramatic U-shaped glacial valley.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for the winding climb to Glen Alps; conditions vary
days.note: Bear safety protocol is essential; carry deterrents and follow official NPS/State Park guidance.

days.title: Turnagain Arm and Glacial Valleys

stops.name: Beluga Point Site
stops.detail: Stop at this rocky outcrop for views of the Turnagain Arm's bore tide and seasonal whale sightings.

stops.name: Alaska Wildlife Conservation Center
stops.detail: Observe orphaned or injured large mammals like bison and bears in a spacious setting near Portage.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the Seward Highway; traffic and weather may increase duration
days.note: Drivers must focus on the highway; use designated pullouts for all photography.

intel.title: Trailhead Capacity
intel.text: The Glen Alps lot fills very early during sunny summer weekends. Have a backup plan like Kincaid Park if trailhead parking is unavailable.

intel.title: Variable Reception
intel.text: Signal is strong in the city bowl but drops immediately upon entering Chugach valleys or driving south past Potter Marsh. Carry paper maps for any mountain navigation.

intel.title: Southbound Services
intel.text: Fill tanks in Anchorage before heading south on the Seward Highway; services are limited until Girdwood. Ensure your rental has a full spare if exploring beyond paved zones.

intel.title: Daylight Windows
intel.text: Summer offers near-24-hour light, but museum and visitor center hours remain standard. Winter trips require outdoor activities to be compressed between 10 AM and 3 PM.

intel.title: Trail Surface Conditions
intel.text: Many alpine trails remain snow-covered until late June. Check the Alaska State Parks trail report to avoid damaging soft, muddy paths during the spring thaw.

plan.arrival: Pick up your vehicle at Merrill Field (MRI) or Ted Stevens International, then stock up on bear-safe storage and water in Anchorage before heading to your base.
plan.vehicle: RV rentals are popular but check for height restrictions on city streets and specific gravel road bans in rental agreements.
plan.goldenHour: Point Woronzof for sunset views of the inlet, noting that timing varies wildly from summer to winter.
